citation: C. L. Wasson, The [unintelligable]'s new french cook (LOC's transcription of the caption), stereograph, copyright 1903 (the date in the handwritten caption). Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, Stereograph Cards, LC-DIG-stereo-1s44450 (item 2022631775).
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division. Master TIFF 1s44450u.tif (5881 x 3050), read at tile.loc.gov; crops are kept in kevinrhaas/chicago-evidence evidence/people-references-2026-11-06/working_woman_1904/.
locator: The left-hand frame: an older woman standing at the same kitchen table, facing the camera at about three metres, mixing in a bowl.
rights_note: LOC rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on publication.' Published 1903. Used only as a reference picture people are judged against and as the cut of the 1904 working dress (T-3423); nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-06 (T-3423) from the master TIFF. An older woman cook: a dark long-sleeved blouse with a light trimmed yoke, a checked bib apron, a dark spotted skirt to the floor, a dark cloth bound round the hair. The same studio set. The card is one of a comic series; only her working dress is read here. A staged studio photograph, not of Chicago or of any named servant.
note: One of the 1904 working-woman reference set's photographs (data/people_match/reference_sets/working_woman_1904.json).
what_it_supplies: a second working dress of the decade: dark blouse, checked bib apron, long dark skirt
the silhouette of a cook at the table at a few metres
what_it_does_not_supply: anything about Chicago, the Glessner household or Martha Williamson; no likeness is asserted
